# pretest 1.0.6

A scan can no longer run for minutes in silence.

A host that answers the landing page but then stalls on probing cost **296 s**
(and one run passed 400 s) — every one of the 33 artefact probes waited out its
own timeout, and a blackholing host costs one timeout *per address family*. Now:

- artefact probes use an 8 s timeout (a healthy server answers a missing file in ms)
- the sweep stops after 3 consecutive failures, or when a 90 s wall-clock budget
  runs out, and reports that as an `info` finding ("Resten är oprövade — inte rena")

Measured after the change: momento 13 s, example.com 11 s, an unresponsive host 24 s.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

Installs `~/.local/bin/pretest` and verifies the checksum. Or take the file:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py -o pretest.py
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py.sha256 | sha256sum -c -
chmod +x pretest.py
```

## Use

```bash
pretest --url https://example.com
pretest --url https://example.com --domain example.com --repo ~/code/app
pretest --url https://app.example.com -H "Cookie: session=…"   # behind a login
pretest --url https://example.com --fail-on high               # CI gate, exit 1
pretest --self-test                                            # verify the tool
```

## Limits

Not a pentest: no IDOR, no business logic, no injections in your own parameters.
Report text is Swedish, every finding has a stable English `id` in the JSON.
TLS 1.0/1.1 show as *untested* on a modern OpenSSL, not as unsupported. Port
findings behind a CDN describe the CDN edge and say so.
